chapter: The Pelican band and Ridgley years
title: Suburban Garden in Jefferson Parish and Jack Sheen the Coconut King
summary: Sayles and Ridgley open Jack Sheen's new gambling club near the levee until police raids close it, and the interviewer checks what instrument Ridgley played.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Jefferson, yeah. Jefferson, yeah. And this new place, we actually opened that place up. We had gambling and everything. Well, they had one of those things where the sheriff got mad and everything, they'd come in and rage, you know, if he wasn't paying off and see, well, it happened that it got a little hot out there and it got the radio too much and this guy, Jack Sheen, just decided to close down, you see.
Not to interrupt, but what did Ridgely play at that time? What instruments?
Well, at that time, yeah, yeah. Of course, I was told he played bass, he played a little bass, then he went to, well, after playing drum, now that came about later.
Yeah, well, I wanted to straighten that out. Yeah, yeah. The Beverly, the place is now called the Beverly Garden, or it was a few years ago. Maybe it is, but it is, yeah, yeah.
Maybe it is the same place. I know that place was likely built new when we went out there and we made it.
Towards the river from the Jefferson Highway?
Yes, it was not far from the levee.
Because you go out the highway, it was closer to the river.
